title: A paragraph nothing reaches: never PERFORMed, after a GOBACK, its PERFORM commented out
realism: Retired logic stays in place with its PERFORM commented out. A reader that takes the comment for a statement makes the paragraph live.
shapes: ORDMAIN 9000-OLD-RECOVERY: its only PERFORM is a comment line; 0000-MAIN ends in GOBACK
asserts: The paragraph is a unit with its full extent, and it is dead: no PERFORM or GO TO names it, and the paragraph before it is not entered by falling through. A commented PERFORM is no edge.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: Execution begins with the first statement in the PROCEDURE DIVISION, excluding declaratives. Statements are executed in the order in which they are presented for compilation, unless the statement rules dictate some other order of execution.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: The GOBACK statement specifies the logical end of a called program or invoked method.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference (SC27-8713-03)
citations.quote: A comment line is any line with an asterisk (*) or slash (/) in the indicator area (column 7) of the line, or with a floating comment indicator (*>) as the first character-string in the program text area (Area A plus Area B).

compile.reason: COPY ORDPRICE: the estate holds no copybook ORDPRICE (H-0053), so no compiler finds it
compile.check_note: a one-byte FILLER stands in for the missing COPY ORDPRICE

phantoms.why: a PERFORM in a comment line (indicator *) is not a statement
